admin_presence.phone_expl: Phone apps tell this server whether the phone is at home. When everyone has left, the server arms or switches profile; when someone comes back, it switches back. Only those changes act, so arming or switching by hand stays until the next one. No Home Assistant needed.

admin_rules.delete_rule_body: It stops tagging events and sending its alert.
admin_rules.hint_match: Higher is stricter (fewer, surer matches). Around 3 usually means "clearly looks like it"; 0 is no more like the words than any picture. Set it with the test below.
admin_rules.how: Every new event's pictures are compared with the words (the smart search model, on this server's processor); when one matches well enough the event is tagged "rule: name" and the rule's alert is sent with the rule's name: "Delivery truck out front at Front Door". A quiet rule works the other way round: "my own car in the driveway" stops alerts for events that match it. Matching words to pictures is approximate: it can miss, and it can match something that only looks a bit like the words. Use the test to see how recent events scored and set the threshold between the ones you want and the ones you do not. Rules look at events as they happen (not at old ones), and the rule alert comes a few seconds after the ordinary one, once the pictures are checked.
admin_rules.kindhint_alert: An event that matches is tagged "rule: name" and the alert goes out under the rule's name. The ordinary alert for the same event is not replaced: it comes first, this one follows a few seconds later.
admin_rules.kindhint_quiet: An event that matches is tagged "quiet: name" and its alerts are not sent: not the ordinary alert and not another rule's alert. So that this can work, ordinary alerts of the cameras chosen below wait up to the seconds set here for the event's pictures to be checked (other cameras' alerts are never delayed); if they are not checked in time the alert goes out as usual. Events are still recorded, listed and sent over MQTT.

cameras.also_burn_help: Off: the app draws the text, which costs nothing. On: the text becomes part of the video files too (without text set: name, date and time). This re-encodes the camera's video (on the graphics card when it has a video encoder that passed the test at start, else on the processor: about one core per 4K camera) and turns off smooth live view for this camera: Live and the apps fall back to a snapshot that refreshes, with no sound. Leave it off unless the files themselves must carry the text.
cameras.also_trigger_hint: When this camera detects motion, these record an event too (each with its own pre- and post-roll). Off unless you tick something. Cameras that are only triggered never pass it on.
cameras.any_flv: Any FLV stream (H.264 or H.265 video, AAC audio) sent with PUT or POST works. The port opens automatically when you save.
cameras.asleep_tip: A battery camera asleep to save power. It wakes for motion or when you open it.
cameras.at_least_db_hint: How loud in itself: 0 is the loudest the microphone reports, a quiet room is about -60.
cameras.audio_hint: Sound in the live view and in recordings, when the camera sends it.
cameras.break_time_hint: An event ends only after this long without motion.
cameras.bulk_admin_needed: Editing several cameras at once needs an admin sign-in
cameras.bulk_hint: A field that differs between these cameras says Mixed and is left alone. Change a field and it is set on all of them; nothing else is touched. Name, groups, stream, sign-in, zones and sounds are per camera, so they are edited one at a time.
cameras.camera_own_detection: Camera's own detection needs AI to agree
cameras.camera_own_hint: When the camera itself reports a person, vehicle or animal, it alerts only if AI sees one too (AI keeps looking while the camera reports). Doorbell presses, sounds and packages always count. If AI cannot look, the camera's word counts. Off: the camera's own detection alerts on its own.
cameras.card_found: Card found ({gb} GB). Holes are filled from its {stream} stream.
cameras.clips_also_saved: event clips also saved to a folder
cameras.clips_hint: Each event's clip is also saved here as an .mp4 a few seconds after it ends, in folders by camera and date. In a folder OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox syncs, events are off-site within minutes. Recording does not change. The full path of an existing folder; empty = off.
cameras.comma_separated: Comma separated, e.g. person, car, dog.
cameras.connect_hint: For always-on Reolink cameras, not battery cameras. Auto moves to RTSP after port 9000 fails 3 times or sends no video for 2 minutes, and tries port 9000 again every 30 minutes. A wrong password stops both. Burned-in text keeps the camera on RTSP.

cameras.direct_copy_hint: Saves the camera's own video without re-encoding (lowest CPU).

cameras.doorbell_always: Doorbell presses, sounds and packages always notify. Other objects are still detected, recorded and searchable; they just don't send a notification.

cameras.fill_gaps: Fill gaps from the camera's card
cameras.fill_gaps_desc: When the camera drops off (Wi-Fi, a router restart, AmberSight restarting) and is back, the missing part is copied from its memory card and appears on the timeline marked as from the card. Reolink cameras with a card, recording continuously. Holes up to 2 hours.
cameras.folder_placeholder: Folder, e.g. a OneDrive or Google Drive folder
cameras.forget_msg: This happens right now, not when you press Save. {name} forgets every spot it has learned and every spot marked not real, so what AI sees there alerts again until it learns them again. Recordings and past events are not touched.
cameras.forgot_n: {n, plural, one {Forgot # spot} other {Forgot # spots}}: what AI sees there alerts again.
cameras.groups_hint: A camera can be in several groups. Click a group to add or remove it; type a new name and press Enter.
cameras.hide_unconfirmed_hint: Motion where AI found none of the objects that count (a flag or branches in the wind, or only an umbrella) stays out of Events and the timeline. Nothing is deleted and recording is unaffected; Events can still show them.
cameras.hw_decode_help: How motion detection decodes the picture. Auto follows Settings, System, Hardware (by default NVIDIA first, then Intel Quick Sync, then VAAPI, among the ways that passed a test decode at start; else the processor). A way that fails later is replaced at once and tried again later.
cameras.ignore_parked_hint: A car parked in view (or someone sitting still) for a few minutes no longer confirms every motion event; one that arrives or leaves still does. AI also remembers spots where the same kind of thing is seen event after event (a bush or a bin it takes for a person, a parked car): they stop alerting until they move or go.
cameras.ignore_unmoved: Ignore objects that have not moved
cameras.import_missed: Import missed events from the camera's card
cameras.import_missed_desc: When a push is missed (push off in the Reolink app, Wi-Fi or DNS trouble) or AmberSight was down, the camera still records to its card. Its recordings of the last 12 hours that AmberSight has no event for are imported as events, marked "from card". Events older than a few minutes send no notification. Each look wakes the camera.
cameras.keep_copies_desc: 0 = keep them. Only the clips and pictures AmberSight saved there are deleted.
cameras.key_private: The key is the password for sending to this camera. Keep it private.

cameras.list_hint_touch: {n, plural, one {# camera} other {# cameras}}. Tap a camera's gear for its settings.
cameras.local_hint: Raw video is encoded to H.264 for recording, which uses CPU. On Windows, the AmberSight service runs in session 0 and cannot capture the screen; some cameras (virtual ones especially) also refuse to open there. Run AmberSight in your own session (ambersight run) for those.
cameras.look_at_card_hint: Always after AmberSight starts, after the camera was unreachable, and after a push that brought no recording. If the camera stays asleep, it is woken to look at most every three times the period.
cameras.looking_sub_stream: Looking for the sub stream (this can take a few seconds)...
cameras.loud_starts_event: A loud sound starts an event
cameras.loud_starts_event_desc: A sudden sound much louder than usual here (glass, a bang, a shout, a dog) is recorded and alerts like motion, in the same arm window. The camera must send sound; the Audio setting can stay off.
cameras.louder_by_hint: Lower hears quieter sounds, and gives more false alarms.
cameras.make_new_key: Make a new key (senders using the old one stop working)
cameras.max_object_hint: Larger changes are treated as lighting changes.
cameras.min_frames_hint: Frames in a row with motion before an event starts.
cameras.min_object_help: The smallest moving object that counts. Lower notices smaller things (and more false alarms).
cameras.min_travel_hint: How far something must move before it counts. Filters swaying branches.
cameras.mixed_hint: These cameras differ. Pick a level to set it on all of them.
cameras.mixed_tick: Mixed: tick to set the same window on all
cameras.monitor_hint: Blank captures the whole desktop. A number picks one monitor (0 = first; Windows).

cameras.off_events: Off: events are still recorded and still reported over MQTT, just not sent anywhere.
cameras.off_stops_tip: Off stops live view and recording; old footage is kept
cameras.only_confirmed_hint: Only events with a person, vehicle or other object AI confirmed, a sound, or the camera's own detection (with AI off: every event). Notification settings never leave a copy out. Off: every event.

cameras.onvif_unavailable: This camera doesn't offer ONVIF, so AmberSight can't move it. Some firmware has an ONVIF switch in the camera's own app.

cameras.outlet_hint: 0 = the first (most plugs have just one).
cameras.overlay_hint: Drawn by the app over this camera's live view and playback (playback shows the recording's own date and time), and put into its snapshots, event pictures and time-lapse frames. Downloads carry the time as subtitles, or the text itself when "Burn the text into this clip" is on. Fill-ins: {fname}, {fshort} (short name), {fsite} (this server), {fdate}, {ftime}, and {fv} for a value an automation sends in (weather or a temperature from Home Assistant, for example) over MQTT (<prefix>/overlay/NAME/set) or POST /api/overlay/NAME. Empty = no text. {fv} shows in live view only.
cameras.package_hint: For doorbells: after someone has been at the door, AmberSight compares the picture from before the visit with one a little after. Something new that looks like a box, parcel or mailer is a delivery ("Package at ..." alert, event and Home Assistant sensor); when it is gone after a later visit, "Package picked up". Uses the smart search picture model (downloaded the first time).
cameras.pause_msg: {name}: no notifications for a while. It is still recording, detecting motion and listing events (and MQTT still reports them).

cameras.priority_hint: For ntfy and Pushover. High usually gets through Do Not Disturb; urgent makes Pushover repeat until you acknowledge it.

cameras.record_mode_hint: The middle choice keeps the full picture only around events and the sub stream the rest of the time, using far less space. It needs a sub stream URL; without one the camera records continuously.

cameras.strangers_days_desc: Up to 60: unnamed faces are forgotten after 60 days.
cameras.strangers_first_alert: Alert only the first time an unknown person or vehicle appears
cameras.strangers_first_desc: Someone or something unknown that was already seen in the last days stays quiet. Needs faces / plates on.
cameras.strangers_hint: Alert only when the person or vehicle is not known. cameras.strangers_off_default: Off by default. The alert for this camera waits a few seconds for the faces to be looked at.
cameras.strangers_only_unknown: Only alert for unknown people and vehicles
cameras.strangers_schedule_desc: Leave off to use this filter all day. With hours, it applies only inside them.
cameras.stream_url_format: Stream URL must start with rtsp:// (or another stream address such as http://).
cameras.strict_hint: Alert only when AI sees the object in 2 of 3 looks in a row and it moved between them. Fewer false alerts; someone passing very quickly may be missed.

cameras.test_cycle_done: Done: the power went off and on again.
cameras.things_here_detected: Things here are still detected, recorded and searchable. They just don't send a notification.
cameras.transport_auto: Auto (TCP; UDP when the camera refuses TCP)
cameras.transport_hint: How the video travels from the camera. Auto uses TCP, the most reliable; a camera that answers "461 Unsupported Transport" (it offers only UDP) is asked again over UDP, and UDP is kept for it. Pick UDP only for such a camera: UDP loses pictures on a busy or Wi-Fi network.

It is worked out on this server from its own events; nothing leaves it. Each highlight links to its event. Push messages are short and link to the full summary page; email gets a richer version with pictures.
digest.lead_main: One message a day about what happened at your cameras overnight.
digest.lead_sub: Turn it on, send it at about the time you wake up, and skip quiet days.
digest.no_message_quiet: No message on a quiet day.

help.admin_ai_download_a_detection: Download a detection model (it runs on this server; pictures never leave it): Tiny is the lightest, Small (recommended) suits most, and Large is the most accurate but takes about five times the work per check, so it needs a graphics card to keep up with several cameras. The page shows the measured time per check for the model in use. If the graphics card gives errors, the failed checks are done again later on the saved pictures, and after three errors in a row the AI runs on the processor for 5 minutes before trying the card again. Or use an AI server you already run. Choose the objects that confirm an event, the minimum confidence (lower finds more, and more false alarms) and whether parked objects are ignored. Cameras can turn AI off or use their own objects.
help.admin_aireview_what_ai_saw: What AI saw in each motion event and why it did or did not alert. "Almost" means it saw something wanted but was not sure enough: worth a look if alerts are missing. Many "Nothing found" usually means shadows, lights or bugs: raise the camera's motion thresholds or add an ignore zone. Open an event for its frames and one-click fixes. "Same spot" means what AI saw has been in that spot in several earlier events, or you marked it not real there (see Camera: AI). A filter above the list (Camera only, Parked ...) looks through the whole period, not only the latest events.
help.admin_alertrules_a_quiet_rule: A quiet rule ("my own car in the driveway") tags matching events "quiet: name" and stops their alerts, the ordinary one and other rules' alerts alike. To make that possible, ordinary alerts of the cameras a quiet rule covers wait up to the seconds set for the pictures to be checked; if they are not checked in time they go out as usual. Cameras without a quiet rule are never delayed. If a quiet rule drops an alert, the event's AI review says so. A rule's own alert is not sent for an event whose ordinary alert was kept quiet because the person was known (strangers only, or a person marked "no alerts"). Events are still recorded and listed. Rules work only while smart search is on, and look at events as they happen, not at old ones.
help.admin_alertrules_test_against_recen: Test against recent events shows the recent events that look most like your words with their scores; green ones would have matched at the current threshold. Move the threshold between the events you want and the ones you do not, then save. The match is approximate: it can miss, and it can match something that only looks a bit like the words.
help.admin_alertrules_write_what_should: Write what should alert you in words, such as "a delivery truck stopped out front" or "a person carrying a box on the porch", and choose the cameras, a time window and what happens: an alert (normal or high priority), a quiet notice, or only a tag on the event. Every new event's pictures are compared with the words; a match tags the event "rule: name" and sends the alert under the rule's name ("Delivery truck out front at Front Door"). It comes a few seconds after the ordinary alert, once the pictures are checked, and the same rule alerts again for a camera only after the number of minutes set.
help.admin_audit_who_signed_in: Who signed in and who changed what, and when.
help.admin_discovery_finds_cameras_on: Finds cameras on the network (ONVIF), tries the login you give (most people use one login for all their cameras; at most two tries each so cameras do not lock you out), and adds them with their main and sub streams. If a camera refuses the login over ONVIF, Find cameras also tries the Dahua-style video stream with it (Dahua, Amcrest and brands that sell their cameras); when that works the camera is added without ONVIF events. On some of these cameras ONVIF might need to be turned on, or might need its own user. Cameras on another subnet need that address range filled in.
help.admin_faces_click_a_face: Click a face under Faces to name to say who it is; ticking "also name faces that look like this one" names the look-alikes too. A few clear faces of each person (daylight and night) make it much more reliable. Import named faces reads a folder with one sub-folder per person. For each person you can turn on No alerts when only they are seen: such events are kept but send no alert. Faces nobody names are forgotten after 60 days, or with their event; Forget deletes a person and every picture of their face. Face pictures live in this server's database and backups, and names appear in alerts. A photo can fool face recognition, so do not rely on 'no alerts' for security.
help.admin_faces_when_ai_sees: When AI sees a person, AmberSight looks for a face in the full-quality recording and compares it with the faces you have named; the event is labeled with the name, or "unknown face". It works best on doorbells and cameras that see people close and front-on; faces smaller than the size set are skipped. Turn it on here (it downloads two small models, about 39 MB, that run on this server).
help.admin_logs_the_server_s: The server's recent warnings and errors, newest first. Useful when a camera keeps reconnecting or a notification does not arrive.
help.admin_lpr_it_works_best: It works best on a camera that sees plates close, straight on and lit, such as a driveway or gate camera; a plate under about 50 pixels wide (in the recording) is skipped, and you can change that and how sure a reading must be, for every camera or one. Whole picture makes a camera look for plates in the whole frame when AI saw no vehicle (a camera aimed at a gate).
help.admin_lpr_known_plates_are: Known plates are the cars you have named, with optional notes. A reading matches one when it is the same plate, or one character different, or differs only in look-alike characters (O and 0, I and 1, B and 8 ...); change that under Matching. Name a plate from Seen lately with Add to known, or from the event itself. Search the event list for a plate (or part of one) to find its events; the same readings go to Home Assistant over MQTT ("Last plate" and a "Plate" event, known or unknown).
help.admin_lpr_plate_pictures_and: Plate pictures and readings stay in the database; unknown plates are forgotten after 6 months, known ones stay. Do not rely on a plate alone for security: plates can be copied or misread.
help.admin_lpr_when_ai_sees: When AI sees a car, truck or motorcycle that is not parked, AmberSight finds its plate in the full-quality recording, reads it, and labels the event: "plate ABC123 (Mom's car)" for a plate you have named, "unknown plate ABC123" for any other. The alert says which car it was. Several frames are read and the surest reading is kept. Turn it on here (plates are found by a model built into AmberSight and read by a small free model, about 5 MB, that downloads once; both run on this server's processor), then switch on the cameras that see plates.
help.admin_presence_phone_apps_signed: Phone apps signed in to this server can report whether the phone is at home. When every phone that reported recently is away for the chosen number of minutes, the server arms (or switches to the away profile); when one comes back it switches to the home profile, or back to the schedule, and disarms if you ticked that. Only these changes act: arming or switching by hand stays until the next one. A home profile stays until changed by hand or the next time everyone leaves; leaving replaces a profile chosen by hand. A phone that has not reported within the set hours is not counted; with no phone counting nothing happens then, and the server remembers who was last home or away (also across restarts), so coming back after a long trip still acts. You can pick which accounts' phones count (none ticked: all); other accounts cannot report. Any counted phone coming back triggers the home actions. Each account reports its own phones; admins see and remove all of them here. For app makers, see the API guide (Presence).
help.admin_profiles_a_profile_e: A profile (e.g. Home, Away, Night) changes chosen camera settings: motion, alerts, AI, recording, motion only. Rules switch profiles by time of day, sunrise or sunset; the first rule covering the moment wins, otherwise the default profile applies. You can also pick a profile by hand for a while from the side panel.
help.admin_status_how_the_server: How the server is doing. The banner at the top says everything is OK only when every card below it is OK; otherwise it lists each thing to check in a few words, with the button that helps. Storage counts the archive folder too: the days kept are those of a folder together with the archive it moves old recordings to. A battery camera that is asleep is counted as asleep, not as offline. Per camera: bitrate, how much it records per day and how far back its recordings go. Per folder: how many days it holds at the measured rate. Below that, recent warnings and errors. To see which cameras use the most space, look at their per-day figures; switching a camera to "sub stream, main stream around events" usually cuts its share sharply. The Updates row under the cards shows new versions of AmberSight and installs them (see Updates).
help.admin_status_the_connections_tab: The Connections tab lists the browsers and apps of the last hour and Transcoding for players: the video encoders found and each stream being converted for an app that cannot play it as it is (camera, size, encoder, viewers, CPU). An app gets the sub stream instead when every place is in use; NVIDIA consumer cards allow only a few encodes at a time. [transcode] encoder = "off" in the config turns converting off.
help.admin_storage_also_record_the: Also record the sub stream: a small second copy of continuous cameras (about a tenth more space) for phones with Data saver on. Keep event footage first: when deleting, quiet footage goes before footage around events from the last N days (0 = off). Every drive also keeps 2% free (at least 1 GB) whatever the caps say. Protected events are never deleted.
help.admin_storage_keep_this_folder: Keep this folder private (each extra folder): only administrators and AmberSight can open it, so browsing it in File Explorer or over a network share may stop working. It is applied in the background (a folder with many recordings can take several minutes; recording carries on) and the line under the switch shows whether it is private, open, being applied or could not be applied. It is on by default for a new or empty folder and off for one that already holds files; folders you added before are not changed until you switch them. A whole drive cannot be made private: choose a folder on it. Network drives and FAT or exFAT drives cannot be made private. Turning it off asks first, because the folder then gets what its parent allows, which may let other accounts open it again. Above the folders, the data folder (and on Windows the program folder) show their own state, read-only, with the reason when one was left alone.
help.admin_storage_where_recordings_go: Where recordings go. Cameras record into the data folder unless their setup picks another folder (another drive or a network share). Each folder can have a cap; when a folder is full, its oldest recordings move to the archive folder if there is one, otherwise they are deleted. A full folder that hands its oldest to the archive is working as intended, not a warning.
help.admin_users_accounts_and_what: Accounts and what they may do. Each has a role. A viewer watches live video, events and recordings. An operator can also do the day-to-day things ticked for them: move PTZ cameras, talk and record clips, arm and disarm (and switch profiles and pause notifications), keep events and mark them, and change the detection and alert settings of their cameras. Untick what someone should not do. An admin can do everything, including settings and users. Viewers and operators can be limited to some cameras (none ticked = all); an operator then controls only those, and cannot arm, disarm or switch profiles (those change every camera). Making an operator, or giving one more rights, asks for your own password, and every change an operator makes to a camera is reported to the admins. A sign-in code lets a device sign in once without typing the password (one use, 10 minutes). There must always be at least one admin.
help.arming_profiles_and_schedules: Profiles and schedules (Settings › Schedules & presence) can arm and disarm by themselves, for example when everyone leaves.
help.arming_the_button_in: The button in the header (and S) switches motion detection for every camera at once. Armed (green): cameras look for motion, record events and send alerts. Disarmed (red): no motion detection and no new events, but continuous recordings carry on. Arming can wait a few seconds so you can leave (Arming in 30 s; tap again to cancel). After disarming a message offers Undo for a few seconds.
help.away_from_home_the_simplest_and: The simplest and safest way is a private network app such as Tailscale on the server and on your phone: then the same address works everywhere and nothing is opened to the internet. Turn on HTTPS (Settings › Users & security › HTTPS) so the sign-in and the video are encrypted, and add a password (Settings › Users & security › Users) before you reach it from outside. Alerts reach your phone anywhere once set up in Settings › Detection & alerts › Alerts.
help.bookmarks_a_bookmark_marks: A bookmark marks a moment with a short note (up to 500 characters), on one camera or on all of this server's cameras. On the timeline press B or the bookmark button: the note is for the moment at the playhead. Pick All cameras or one camera, and tick Keep video (for all cameras this is for admins; at most 200 bookmarks may keep video) to hold the recordings from 2 minutes before to 2 minutes after the moment back from automatic cleanup (age and size limits), like a kept event. Recording never stops for them: only when the drive is full and nothing else is left, kept video is deleted too, oldest first, and admins are alerted. Unticking Keep, deleting the bookmark or removing its camera lets them go again. Settings › Recording shows how much they hold.
help.bookmarks_admins_and_operators: Admins and operators with the Events right add bookmarks; operators change or delete their own, admins any. Everyone sees the bookmarks of the cameras they may see, and the all-cameras ones (also accounts limited to some cameras).
help.bookmarks_bookmarks_show_as: Bookmarks show as amber flags on the strip (filled when the video is kept, a dashed line for all cameras); hover for the note, click to play from there, edit, delete or export the 4 minutes around it. Bookmarks (on the timeline's second row, or Ctrl K) lists them newest first: search the notes, pick a camera, click one to play it.
help.camera_ai_camera_s_own: Camera's own detection needs AI to agree (off unless you turn it on): when the camera itself reports a person, vehicle or animal, it alerts only if AI sees one too; AI keeps looking while the camera reports. If AI cannot look, the camera's word counts. Doorbell presses, sounds and packages always count. The AI review says “the camera itself reported ..., but AI did not see one”.
help.camera_ai_not_a_person: Not a person (or Not a car ...) under the AI verdict of an event AI got wrong marks it not a real alert and remembers the spot of what sat still in it, at once, for 30 days, unless it is seen moving. Something that moved in that event (someone walking) is never remembered, and with only one AI look in the event nothing is (too little to tell what stood still). Not a real alert alone only marks the event. Taking the mark back forgets it. Switching to another AI model (or AI server) starts the remembered spots and these marks over on every camera: they are where that model drew its boxes.
help.camera_ai_remembered_spots_with: Remembered spots (with Ignore objects that have not moved on): when AI sees the same kind of thing in the same spot in 3 separate events within a day (a bush or a bin it takes for a person, a car parked across the street), that spot stops alerting. For a person- or animal-shaped one it also has to have been seen there in two other events only with low confidence, which a real person seldom is; a person-shaped thing bigger than a small, far-off box is never held. Anything that moves there, or is clearly bigger or smaller, still alerts, and so does everything elsewhere in the picture. A remembered spot lasts a day, then has to be learned again; a spot not seen for a day is forgotten. A car in a remembered spot is held only if the spot was last seen with a car in it when the event began; if it was last seen empty, the car is an arrival and alerts. When something else in the picture confirms an event, AI stops looking, so a parked car may drive off unseen: the next car in that spot then alerts once. A second car on a parked car's spot (one driving past in front of it) alerts. The event is still recorded, labeled and searchable; its AI review says “has been in that spot in several earlier events”. The camera's AI settings show how many spots it remembers, next to the AI on/off and the objects, with Forget remembered spots (it asks first and acts at once, not when you press Save).
help.camera_ai_with_ai_on: With AI on, a motion event alerts only when AI sees one of the objects that count (e.g. person, car, dog) with at least the minimum confidence; other events are still recorded, just quiet. Ignore objects that have not moved: a parked car does not confirm every event; one arriving or leaving does. Stricter confirmation: the object must be seen in 2 of 3 looks in a row and have moved between them (fewer false alerts; someone passing very quickly may be missed). Blank values use Settings › Detection & alerts › Objects (AI).
help.camera_alert_zones_area_alerts_when: Area: alerts when an object of the chosen kinds stays inside longer than the time you set (loitering), once per visit. Line: alerts when an object's feet cross it. The arrow shows which way is in (the right-hand side walking from A to B); choose In, Out or Both. A small distance past the line is needed, so a wobbling box at the line does not count.
help.camera_alert_zones_cost_while_there: Cost: while there is motion (and while someone still stands in an area, for a while), AmberSight looks at the picture about every 0.7 seconds to follow people and cars. Settings › Detection & alerts › Objects has the look interval and how long to keep watching someone who stands still. Slower looks cost less but follow fast movers badly; a look is never started while the previous one is still running.
help.camera_alert_zones_each_zone_has: Each zone has its own objects, Send alerts, Save events (with a clip) and an optional time window. Events are tagged like loitering: Driveway or crossed: Gate (in): search for them in Events, and they appear in alerts, MQTT (a sensor per area, an event per line in Home Assistant) and the camera's zone topic. Alerts follow the arm state and profiles like other alerts, and are not held back by the alert interval.
help.camera_alert_zones_ignore_parked_ve: Ignore parked vehicles (on by default): a car or truck that has sat in the same place for a few minutes does not count, so a parked car does not alert on every motion. It uses the AI setting 'Ignore objects that have not moved', which must be on for the camera.
help.camera_alert_zones_in_edit_zones: In Edit zones, pick Alert area or Alert line, draw on the picture and name it. AI object checks must be on (Settings › Detection & alerts › Objects); the zones work on what the AI sees, and the object's feet (the bottom center of its box) decide where it is.
help.camera_alert_zones_title: Camera: Alert zones (loitering and line crossing)
help.camera_alerts_whether_this_camera: Whether this camera sends notifications, to which services (all by default), during which hours, at most how often, and at which priority. Off still records events and reports them over MQTT; it just sends nothing. The services themselves are set up in Settings › Detection & alerts › Alerts.
help.camera_av_also_burn_it: Also burn it into recordings (under More settings) makes the text part of the video files too. Without it the text already shows everywhere in AmberSight at no cost. On, the video is re-encoded (about one processor core per 4K camera, or the graphics card), and smooth live view for that camera is off (Live and the apps fall back to a snapshot that refreshes, with no sound), so leave it off unless the files themselves must carry it.
help.camera_av_audio_sound_in: Audio: sound in the live view and recordings, when the camera sends it. Text on the picture: your own text in a corner, with fill-ins '{'name'}', '{'short'}', '{'site'}', '{'date'}', '{'time'}', and '{'v:NAME'}' for a value an automation pushes in (weather, a temperature from Home Assistant, and the like) over MQTT (<prefix>/overlay/NAME/set) or POST /api/overlay/NAME. The app draws it over live view and playback (playback shows the recording's own date and time; a '{'v:NAME'}' value shows in live view only), and it is put into snapshots, event pictures and time-lapse frames. Downloads carry the time as a subtitle track (except an event clip sent from its saved clip file as it is, with nothing to burn in); Burn the text into this clip (where clips are saved) draws the text into the file, which takes longer.
help.camera_general_name_and_a: Name and a short name for places where space is tight; groups it belongs to (several are fine); Enabled: a disabled camera is not connected, recorded or shown.
help.camera_masks_ambersight_does_not: AmberSight does not make privacy masks. Use the camera's own privacy mask if it has one (Reolink, Dahua/Amcrest and Hikvision cameras do): the area never leaves the camera, so it is missing from every picture, recording and stream, and it costs nothing here.
help.camera_masks_on_a_camera: On a camera that had masks before 0.11.2, each mask became an ignore zone and an area that doesn't notify: objects there are still found and searchable, but ordinary object alerts there are not sent. Masks that didn't fit in those lists were left out, and Status says how many. Sharing (RTSP) of those cameras was turned off, because their picture now includes the areas the masks hid; turn Share back on if you want a camera shared.
help.camera_masks_to_keep_motion: To keep motion in an area from counting (a neighbor's window, a road), draw an ignore zone in Edit zones. It only stops motion there from counting: the area is still in the picture and the recordings.
help.camera_motion_values_left_blank: Values left blank use Settings › Detection & alerts › Motion sensitivity. Arm window limits detection to certain hours (e.g. 20:00-07:00). To cut false alarms: raise min object size (small things), contrast (shadows, noise) or min travel (swaying branches), or draw zones.
help.camera_motion_zones_on_the: Zones: on the Live page, open a camera's menu and choose Draw a motion zone (or use Edit zones in its settings). Motion only counts inside a detect zone, and never inside an ignore zone. Nothing is saved until you press Save. Event break time: how long without motion before an event ends.
help.camera_recording_also_save_event: Also save event clips to: the camera keeps recording as set above, and each event's clip is also saved as an .mp4 in this folder a few seconds after the event (and its post-roll) ends, as Camera\2026-11-13\14-03-22 person, car.mp4 with its picture beside it. Point it at a folder that OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox syncs and events are off-site within minutes; no second camera and no second stream are needed. Files are written under a temporary .part name and renamed when complete, so sync apps normally see only finished clips. Only events AI confirmed leaves out events where AI found nothing that counts (with AI off every event is copied); notification settings (alerts off, alert hours, pauses, limits, Notify only for, areas that don't notify) never leave a copy out. Loitering, line-crossing and package events are not copied separately: the motion event they come from is. Keep copies deletes copies older than that many days (0 = keep them); only the clips and pictures AmberSight saved there are touched. A renamed camera starts a new folder; its old one is not trimmed any more. The folder does not count toward the space for recordings and recording clean-up never deletes there; AmberSight stops copying while that drive has less than 2 GB (or 5%) free, 10 GB (or 10%) on the system drive or the drive of its own data.
help.camera_recording_continuous_sub_str: continuous: sub stream, main stream around events: the sub stream all the time and the full-quality main stream only around events, including the pre-roll (kept in memory). Uses far less space: often a tenth. Playback shows full quality wherever it was recorded. Needs a sub stream; without one the camera records continuously.
help.camera_recording_continuous_the_mai: continuous: the main stream all the time.
help.camera_recording_fill_gaps_from: Fill gaps from the camera's card: when a Reolink camera with a memory card drops off and is back, the missing part (20 seconds to 2 hours, up to 12 hours ago) is copied from its card and added to the recordings. A thin amber line under the timeline marks what came from the card. Offered only when the camera answers with a card in it; it needs continuous recording. The picture starts at the card's next keyframe, so a few seconds can stay empty. Tested on one Reolink Duo Floodlight WiFi v2; other models are untested.
help.camera_recording_import_missed_even: Import missed events from the camera's card (battery Reolink cameras without a hub): the camera records to its card even when AmberSight misses its motion message (push off in the Reolink app, Wi-Fi or DNS trouble, AmberSight stopped). Its recordings of the last 12 hours that AmberSight has no event for are imported as events: recording, thumbnail and AI check, marked from card in the event list and with the amber line on the timeline. An event that ended more than 5 minutes before it was imported sends no notification. Each look wakes the camera, so it looks after a start, after the camera was unreachable, after a motion message that brought no recording, and otherwise at most hourly while the camera is awake anyway (Look at the card). Nothing is imported from times the camera was disarmed or not recording. On by default for battery cameras; not yet tried on a real camera.
help.camera_recording_pre_roll_and: Pre-roll and post-roll are the seconds kept before an event starts and after it ends (blank = the default in Settings › Detection & alerts › Motion sensitivity). Battery camera: connect only when someone watches, an event happens or the camera reports activity, then disconnect after the idle time.
help.camera_recording_the_folder_must: The folder must exist; AmberSight never creates it, so an unplugged drive or an offline share is noticed. It may not be a temporary folder or one anyone on the computer may change (Linux, macOS), and two cameras with the same name cannot save to the same folder. Pick a folder other users of the computer cannot rename or delete (inside your own user folder, such as your OneDrive folder); if the folder is later replaced by another one at the same path, copies stop with “the copy folder was replaced” until you press Test, which accepts it. Test checks that AmberSight can write there. While the folder is missing or cannot be written, copies wait (up to 3 days) and are made when it is back; if it keeps failing, a system problem is reported (Settings › Detection & alerts › Alerts, System problems) with the reason. On Windows the AmberSight service runs as the Local System account: if it may not write to a folder in your user folder, give that account access (folder Properties, Security) or use a folder outside your user folder that your sync app syncs. The service does not see mapped drive letters (Z:): use the share's own name (\\nas\share\cameras).
help.camera_stream_a_camera_with: A camera with no sub stream makes motion detection decode the full-size picture. For a large one (4K, 8 MP) on the processor the Stream section and Status say so (a note, not a problem), and Find the sub stream looks for it (the camera's ONVIF profiles, or the usual address for its make); you confirm before it is saved. A camera with only one stream: Don't warn about this camera turns the note off.
help.camera_stream_a_network_camera: A network camera is entered in parts: the camera address (like 192.168.1.50), its port and protocol (RTSP, RTSPS, HTTP or HTTPS), the camera's own user name and password, and the path of each stream. The main stream is what gets recorded and shown full size. An optional sub stream (lower resolution) is used for motion detection and the Live grid, which saves a lot of CPU; most cameras have one. A path can be typed with or without its leading /; a query such as ?channel=1&subtype=1 is part of it. Under the fields, the form shows the full addresses it saves.
help.camera_stream_ambersight_reads_rtsp: AmberSight reads RTSP cameras itself; one it cannot play after a few tries is switched to ffmpeg automatically (a camera that is merely off or rebooting is not). Burned-in text (Also burn it into recordings) also needs ffmpeg. Receiving says which reader the camera uses and why; on ffmpeg, a camera with a sub stream decodes it for motion and records the main stream separately. The analysis frame rate and width set how much CPU motion detection uses.
help.camera_stream_brand_fills_both: Brand fills both paths with the usual ones for that make (the ones we tested are listed first; the camera guide has the details). A battery Reolink Argus with no hub has no stream paths: pick Reolink battery (Argus, no hub), then type its address and its UID (Reolink app, Device info), and Battery camera is turned on for you (on a camera added before, click Use battery settings). Its motion message always starts an event, whatever the camera's trigger setting. Push notifications must be on for the camera in the Reolink app, or it sends no motion message. Find via ONVIF asks the camera itself for its stream paths with the user name and password typed in; on a saved camera with the password left blank, it looks for the sub stream with the saved sign-in. Pasting a whole address (rtsp://user:pass@192.168.1.50:554/stream1) into the address or a path field splits it into the fields, the password included.
help.camera_stream_camera_report_network: Camera report (Network section, admins): saves a text file for a bug report about the camera: what it sends (its RTSP description and what ffmpeg finds in each stream), its ONVIF profiles, how AmberSight reads it and why, and its recent log lines. User names and passwords are removed. It takes up to 20 seconds. Attach it to a GitHub issue. It also says why a camera is read by ffmpeg (overlay, ingest setting) and, on Linux, the process limit of the server or container. A camera note about “Resource temporarily unavailable” means that limit was reached (Docker: raise or remove --pids-limit).
help.camera_stream_hardware_decoding_mor: Hardware decoding (More settings): Auto follows the server-wide setting in Settings › System › Hardware (by default an NVIDIA card first, then Intel Quick Sync, then VAAPI, and the processor when none passed a test decode at start). Off always uses the processor; NVIDIA (NVDEC), VAAPI and Quick Sync pick the way for this camera, and the graphics card when there are several. A way that fails while running is replaced at once and tried again later. Status, Cameras shows where each camera decodes (GPU or CPU).
help.camera_stream_rtsp_transport_more: RTSP transport (More settings): Auto uses TCP, and a camera that answers "461 Unsupported Transport" (one that offers only UDP) is asked again over UDP, which is then kept for it until AmberSight restarts. TCP and UDP force one way. UDP can lose pictures on a busy or Wi-Fi network.
help.camera_stream_use_full_addresses: Use full addresses shows the two complete addresses instead, for unusual setups. It is on by itself for a camera whose sub stream is on another address or port, whose address carries its sign-in in the query (Reolink HTTP-FLV), or that uses another protocol (such as baichuan:// or rtmp://). Switching back and forth keeps what is typed.
help.camera_tamper_alerts_when_the: Alerts when the camera is covered (a cloth, tape, paint, a hand), blurred (smeared or sprayed lens, out of focus) or moved (knocked or turned, so the scene no longer matches). Off by default.
help.camera_tamper_ambersight_keeps_a: AmberSight keeps a reference picture for the day (color) and one for the night (gray, infrared), because cameras switch to black and white after dark. It takes each one by itself when the view has been still for a while and refreshes it slowly (about every 6 hours), so daylight, seasons and a new plant do not matter. Set reference now replaces the reference for the light the camera shows right now; use it after you have moved the camera on purpose, or when an alert is about a change that is here to stay.
help.camera_tamper_every_few_seconds: Every few seconds the camera's picture is compared with the reference of the same light. Brightness changes (headlights, sunrise, a cloud, the infrared switch) are ignored; only what the picture shows counts. The wrong view must last the number of seconds you set (60 by default) before you are told, so a person walking close to the camera, a spider or rain do not set it off. You get one alert with the reference and the current picture, and "Camera view restored" once it looks right again for 30 seconds. Sensitivity 1 reports only plain cases, 5 also small changes.
help.camera_tamper_the_alert_follows: The alert follows the camera's Alerts settings (services, priority, pause) and the profile; it is not sent while the system is disarmed. Home Assistant gets a Tamper sensor for the camera. Recent alerts are listed here: click one to see the two pictures. Until the reference for the current light exists (for night, the first quiet night), nothing is judged for that light. A very dark scene with no detail cannot be judged.
help.camera_trigger_also_trigger_when: Also trigger: when this camera detects motion, the cameras or groups ticked here record an event too, each with its own pre- and post-roll. A camera that was only triggered does not pass it on. A camera can also start events from its own detection (person, vehicle, doorbell press) when it reports them.
help.camera_unusual_ambersight_learns_ho: AmberSight learns how often each label (person, car, ... or plain motion) normally happens at this camera in each hour of the week, from the events it has recorded (kept for up to 90 days, longer than the events themselves). An event at an hour when that label almost never happens is flagged: it gets the label unusual (use the Unusual chip in Events to list them) and its notification reads "Unusual: person at Back Gate at 3:12 AM". Off by default.
help.camera_unusual_in_the_alert: In the alert mode an unusual event always alerts at high priority, even on a camera that alerts only for strangers and even for a known person.
help.camera_unusual_it_needs_history: It needs history first: nothing is flagged until the camera has Days of history needed (14 by default) of events, and the page shows "Learning" until then. The pattern looks at the hour before and after too, and at the same hour on other days, so arriving a little early or on a different weekday is not unusual.
help.camera_unusual_labels_it_judges: Labels it judges picks what counts (the default is person). Sensitivity: 1 flags only what has never happened at that hour, 5 also hours that are only a little uncommon. What it does: only mark the event; a quiet notice (low priority); or a full alert (high priority). The grid shows what is normal here for a label, darker for more usual hours.
help.camera_watchdog_test_power_cycle: Test power cycle tries the switch now (the camera goes offline for a minute or two). Reboot camera... in the camera's menu restarts it now. Every restart and power cycle is listed under Recent actions and in Settings › System › Audit.
help.camera_watchdog_when_the_camera: When the camera has had no video for a while (Settings › Connections › Watchdog), AmberSight restarts it through its own interface: ONVIF, or the Reolink, Dahua/Amcrest or Hikvision way (Automatic picks by what the camera is). It signs in with the stream user and password. If the video is still gone 5 minutes later, or the camera does not answer at all, it turns the power switch off and on again (a Shelly or Tasmota plug, or any switch with an off and an on address, such as a PoE switch port). If that does not help either, you get a message to check it by hand.
help.display_mode_display_mode_shows: Display mode shows cameras full screen on a TV, an old tablet or a spare monitor, and keeps running on its own for weeks. Open it from the Layouts menu on Live, with Ctrl K, or bookmark /display on the device.
help.display_mode_it_reconnects_by: It reconnects by itself after a Wi-Fi drop or a server restart and reloads itself after an update. The screen stays on over HTTPS (Settings › Users & security › HTTPS); over plain HTTP set the device's screen timeout to Never.
help.display_mode_it_shows_a: It shows a grid of cameras (all, a saved layout, a group, or the ones you pick). When something happens on one, that camera goes big, stays while it goes on and for some seconds after (20 by default), then the grid comes back; two at once share the screen. Alerts (the default) means what AI confirmed, such as a person or a vehicle (cameras the AI does not check go big on motion); Any motion includes every movement. A clip started with Record now, or by an automation through the API, also brings its camera up. Tap a camera to make it big, tap again (or Esc) to go back.
help.display_mode_move_the_mouse: Move the mouse, tap the screen or press a key on the remote to show Settings: the cameras, what makes one big and for how long, the clock, armed or disarmed and camera names, dimming at night for a bedroom tablet, and the picture (the light pictures or sub streams by default, so an old TV or tablet keeps up). Settings are kept on that device. The clock and labels move a few pixels now and then, so they do not burn into a TV.
help.display_mode_without_a_keyboard: Without a keyboard: a display that is not signed in shows a code. An admin enters it in Settings › Users & security › Displays and picks the account it uses: always a viewer account (make one just for displays, limited to the cameras it should show). The display only shows live cameras (no recordings or events); it stays signed in while it is on, signs out by itself after two weeks unused, and is paired again every six months. Admins get an alert when a display is used from another network. Treat a display like a signed-in phone: someone who can use its browser could copy its sign-in, and a copy works while the real display stays on (only the display itself can keep it signed in). Sign out a lost display from the Displays page. The Displays page lists every display with a Sign out button.
help.download_event_snapshot: Download an event or a snapshot
help.events_everything_the_cameras: Everything the cameras noticed, newest first. Filter by camera, what was detected (person, vehicle, animal, package...) or time (1h, Today, 24h, 7d, Custom). Open an event to play its clip, see what AI found, download it, or keep it forever so retention and a full drive never delete it. Tick events to download several as a ZIP. The number on the Events tab counts events since you last looked.
help.events_follow_it_compares_how: It compares how the person or vehicle looks (shape, colors, clothes or paint) using the smart search model, and is raised when the same recognized face or the same plate was read in both events. This is approximate: someone dressed alike can match, and the same person seen from another angle, in other light or far away can score low. The slider hides weak matches (it starts at 80%); lower it to see more, and look at the pictures before trusting a match. Use the window and "this camera too" to widen the search. It needs smart search to be on, and works on events whose pictures have been searched (older events are done in the background, newest first).
help.events_follow_on_an_event: On an event with a person or vehicle, Follow looks for the same one on other cameras in the minutes before and after, and lists the sightings in time order: camera, time, picture, how well it matches. Tap a sighting to play that camera at that moment, or Follow from here to carry on from it.
help.events_grid_view_the: Grid view: the list/grid control at the top of Events shows the same events as pictures, with the same filters and player. There is no separate Clips tab; old Clips links open the grid.
help.getting_started_a_short_checklist: A short checklist for a new install: add cameras, choose where recordings go, add a sign-in account, use HTTPS, get alerts on your phone and turn on AI. Each step is ticked off by looking at the real setup. Admins see a reminder on Live only while a new install still has no cameras or no sign-in account.
help.home_assistant_with_an_mqtt: With an MQTT broker set, every camera appears in Home Assistant by itself (motion, objects, snapshot, online), plus a server "Problem" sensor that turns on with any system problem. Alerts can also call a Home Assistant service directly (Settings › Detection & alerts › Alerts).
help.live_click_a_tile: Click a tile to select it (the side panel follows it). With a tile selected, the mouse wheel over it zooms that camera only, dragging moves the zoomed picture, and its zoom badge (or scrolling back out) resets it; over any other tile the wheel scrolls the page. The zoom stays until the page is reloaded. Double-click or <kbd>Enter</kbd> opens a tile full size with the main stream and sound (tap Unmute). Full size: arrow keys or swipe for the next camera, the mouse wheel or pinch zooms, drag to pan.
help.live_each_tile_s: Each tile's buttons: snapshot, play back this camera, its clips, record a 20 s clip now, and more (right-click works too). The badges show online/offline, the record mode (REC, REC motion, REC sub+events) and MOTION while something moves.
help.live_every_camera_as: Every camera as a tile, playing its smaller sub stream. The buttons above the grid pick a view style: Grid (equal tiles, scroll for more), Fit (all cameras in the window), Focus and Focus 2 (one or two cameras large). Arrange lets you drag tiles into order; Layouts saves named sets of cameras, tiles per page and order, kept with your account. The group menu shows only one group.
help.live_timeline_cameras_that_record: Cameras that record their sub stream between events play in full quality around events and in the lower sub-stream quality the rest of the time; playback switches between them by itself.
help.live_timeline_l_or_the: <kbd>L</kbd> (or the timeline button) turns the Live page into playback: a strip under the cameras shows what was recorded and the alerts. Click a moment to play every visible camera from exactly there, or press and drag along the strip to scrub (a picture of the moment shows above the pointer); drag the time ruler along the top, scroll sideways or use two fingers to move the strip, and scroll or pinch to zoom; <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses, <kbd>[</kbd> <kbd>]</kbd> change the speed (fast speeds show one picture per few seconds), <kbd>,</kbd> <kbd>.</kbd> jump to the previous or next alert, <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> step 10 s (Shift: 60 s). Hover over the strip (or drag the playhead) for a picture of that moment. Press <kbd>L</kbd> again for live. The calendar button next to Go to opens a month: days with recordings are tinted and days with alerts have a dot (for the cameras shown); click a day to go to the same time of day there, or type an exact time in the Go to field.
help.live_timeline_title: Playback on the Live page (timeline mode)
help.menu_theme_auto_follows: Theme: Auto follows this device (light by day, dark by night if your device does), or choose Light or Dark. Alert pop-ups: show a pop-up in this browser when an alert happens. Keep screen awake: while AmberSight is open and showing, this computer's screen stays on and it does not go to sleep (per device; the browser releases it when the page is hidden or minimized). Start page: what opens when you sign in. Text size: Normal, Large or Larger, for all text on this device. Data saver: Auto (on when the device says the connection is slow or metered), On or Off; with it on, full-size live view uses the smaller sub stream and playback the sub stream's recordings where there are some (Settings › Recording › Drives & folders can keep a copy for every camera). Notifications on this device: camera alerts pop up on this phone or computer like any app's notifications, even with AmberSight closed (no other app needed); it also lists your other devices and sends a test. iPhone and iPad: add AmberSight to the Home Screen first (iOS 16.4 or newer). Change password: at least 8 characters. Trust this server: install this server's own certificate on this device once, so the browser stops warning about HTTPS. Sign out.
help.nothing_matches: Nothing matches. Try fewer or other words.
help.servers_switch_when_servers_are: When servers are linked (Settings › Connections › Servers), the name next to the logo becomes a menu that opens another server, already signed in as the same user. Their cameras can also appear in your Live view (live only; their recordings stay there). Split on the Live toolbar shows two servers side by side.
help.settings_alerts_browser_and_phone: Browser and phone push: browsers turn notifications on themselves. Phone apps that use UnifiedPush deliver through a push server, usually ntfy; Push servers for phone apps lists the ones they may use. ntfy.sh is the public ntfy server; add your own ntfy server's host (host or host:port) to use it. Plain http:// works only for a server on the home network or Tailscale.
help.settings_alerts_set_each_service: Set each service up once; cameras use all of them unless their own Alerts tab picks some. Pictures go to ntfy, Pushover and Telegram; a webhook gets JSON; Home Assistant and a command can run too. The two limits hold back alerts that come too often (per camera, and across all cameras); held-back ones are still recorded. Set this server's address to one your phone can reach so tapping a notification opens the camera at that moment.
help.settings_alerts_system_problems_a: System problems: a camera offline, recordings not being written, a drive nearly full or unreadable. Reported once it has lasted the minutes set, and again when resolved. Send a test checks the services.
help.settings_cameras_all_cameras_add: All cameras. Add by address asks for the stream address (RTSP or HTTP), a local device (webcam, capture card), this computer's screen, or a screen sent from another computer. Settings › Cameras › Find cameras finds cameras on the network for you. Click a camera to change it; Copy to... copies its motion, recording, alert or AI settings to other cameras. Cameras save as you change them.
help.settings_digest_choose_the_time: Choose the time (this server's local time), what it covers (overnight from the time the night starts, the last 24 hours, or since the last summary), the services and the cameras. Phones and browsers get a short message that opens the full summary page; each highlight there opens its event. ntfy and Telegram get a longer text, and email gets a version with pictures. Links in messages need the server's address under Notifications. Skip it when nothing happened sends nothing on a quiet day. Preview shows the next summary without sending; Send a summary now tests the services.
help.settings_digest_one_message_a: One message a day about what happened at your cameras since the last summary: people (known by name, unknown, or with no face seen), vehicles (known plates by name, unknown plates), packages delivered and picked up, loitering and line crossings, tamper alerts, unusual events and cameras that went offline. It is worked out on this server from its own events, with no cloud service. Counts are events, not individual people.
help.settings_groups_groups_organize_cam: Groups organize cameras for the Live view and can be used by other settings (Also trigger, layouts). A camera can be in several. Making a group never turns on recording or triggering by itself.
help.settings_hardware_auto_recommended_: Auto (recommended): the NVIDIA card first while it has memory to spare (below), then Intel or AMD graphics, then the processor.
help.settings_hardware_hardware_decoding: Hardware decoding (Settings › System › Hardware) says where motion detection decodes the picture of cameras whose own Hardware decoding setting is Auto. A change saves at once and applies within seconds, without a restart; a camera with its own setting keeps it.
help.settings_hardware_in_the_config: In the config: [hwdecode] prefer = "auto" (or nvidia, intel, off) and nvidia_min_free_mb = 1536.
help.settings_hardware_keep_free_on: Keep free on the NVIDIA card (1536 MB by default, 0 = off): Auto puts a camera on the NVIDIA card only if this much video memory is still free after it, so the AI and other programs keep room. Cameras that do not fit use Intel or the processor, and move back when 1 GB more is free. Prefer Intel / AMD keeps it too; Prefer NVIDIA and a camera's own NVIDIA setting do not. A camera keeps its place on the card through a short reconnect and gives it up after about 2 minutes offline.
help.settings_hardware_linux_quick_sync: Linux: Quick Sync on Intel Gen12 and newer needs Intel's GPU runtime, a separate package (sudo apt install libmfx-gen1.2 on Debian and Ubuntu, intel-vpl-gpu-rt on Fedora; then restart AmberSight). Without it Quick Sync fails the start-up test and those chips use VAAPI. Windows: an NVIDIA card that passed the test, otherwise the processor. macOS: the processor.
help.settings_hardware_prefer_intel_amd: Prefer Intel / AMD: Intel or AMD graphics first, the NVIDIA card last (useful when the NVIDIA card is busy with AI).
help.settings_hardware_prefer_nvidia_the: Prefer NVIDIA: the NVIDIA card first, with no memory check.
help.settings_hardware_what_auto_tries: What Auto tries, in order: NVIDIA (NVDEC), then Intel Quick Sync and VAAPI, then VAAPI on AMD, then the processor. On Intel from 2020 on (Gen12: Tiger Lake, Rocket Lake, Alder Lake, Arc and later) Quick Sync comes first, because VAAPI there can fail with "Failed to sync surface"; on older Intel VAAPI comes first. At start each way decodes a short H.264 and H.265 sample, and one that fails is never used by Auto (the Start-up test list says why).
help.settings_hardware_when_a_way: When a way fails while running, that camera moves to the next way, or the processor, at once. It tries the failed way again after 15 minutes, then after longer waits (up to 4 hours). A second failure in a row (with no 30 minutes of good running between) makes it leave that way until AmberSight restarts or Hardware decoding or Keep free changes. The NVIDIA card running out of memory is only waited out, never given up for. A way that stopped while the processor then decoded the same stream fine is left alone by every camera for an hour. Per camera shows what each camera uses now and why.
help.settings_https_extra_names_for: Extra names for the certificate: the certificate already covers this computer's addresses, its name and localhost; add any other name you open AmberSight by. Names apply without a restart. The certificate authority is limited (so a stolen key could not be used against other sites): names ending in .lan, .local, .home.arpa or .internal, this computer's name, and home-network and Tailscale (100.x) addresses can always be added. Other names, such as a Tailscale name (nvr.tail1234.ts.net), are only covered by a certificate authority made with them: add them before HTTPS is first turned on, or use your own certificate.
help.settings_https_turning_https_off: Turning HTTPS off: phone apps and bookmarks that use the https:// address must use the http:// address instead; capture helpers, linked servers and the server switcher stop until HTTPS is on again (turning it back on restores them); alert links that use the https:// address must be changed (Settings › Detection & alerts › Alerts); notifications and the microphone stop working. This browser is signed out before the restart, so it can sign in on the http:// address.
help.settings_https_turning_https_on: Turning HTTPS on or off, or changing the certificate files, applies after a restart: Restart now restarts AmberSight (when it runs as a service) and then opens the new address; you sign in again there. Otherwise restart the service by hand. It is refused while an update is being installed. Notifications on a device belong to the address it turned them on at: turn them on again at the new address (account menu, Notifications on this device).
help.settings_https_use_https_encrypts: Use HTTPS encrypts the connection. AmberSight makes its own certificate; nothing is published anywhere. Each device trusts it once (account menu, Trust this server); until then the browser warns that the connection is not private. Browsers only allow notifications, the microphone and keep screen awake on a trusted HTTPS page. Plain http:// addresses on the same port then redirect to https://.
help.settings_https_use_my_own: Use my own certificate (Advanced): the PEM files of a certificate you got elsewhere, full chain and private key, as paths on this server (at most 1 MB each). A renewed certificate is loaded at the next restart. Linked servers and paired capture helpers trust only AmberSight's own certificate authority, so they stop working with your own certificate and cannot be linked or paired again until you switch back. If the files cannot be read when AmberSight starts, it uses its own certificate instead and says so here.
help.settings_motion_the_motion_settings: The motion settings every camera uses unless it sets its own. Choose Low, Medium (the default) or High: High notices smaller and fainter movement, Low ignores more. More settings shows what each choice sets: Smart (recommended) follows moving things and ignores small or jittery changes, Simple fires on the share of the picture that changed; Frames in a row is how long motion must last before an event starts; Keep before motion and Keep after motion are the seconds kept around each event. Only watch during a time window: hours when detection runs (off = all day).
help.settings_odt_runs_your_own: Runs your own detector program on each event picture ('{'image'}' is its file) and adds the objects it prints to the event. Most people use the built-in AI instead (Settings › Detection & alerts › Objects (AI)).
help.settings_servers_link_another_amber: Link another AmberSight server (another site, a cabin) to switch between them signed in as the same user. On one server make a code (Let another server link to this one); on the other enter its address and the code, and check the certificate fingerprint matches. Per link you choose whether to share this server's cameras and whether to show theirs here. Only link servers you control: an admin there can sign in here as any user with the same name.
help.settings_share_only_tcp_is: Only TCP is offered, which Home Assistant, Scrypted, VLC and ffmpeg use or fall back to. The shared video is the camera's own picture, without AmberSight's drawn text. For Home Assistant's Generic Camera also use the Snapshot address as the still image (with the same account in the authentication fields), or the MJPEG address. If a camera is switched off or offline, its shared stream is simply not there until it is back.
help.settings_share_share_streams_lets: Share streams lets other apps (Home Assistant, Scrypted, VLC, another NVR) use AmberSight as their camera source: they connect to AmberSight over RTSP instead of to each camera, so each camera still serves only AmberSight. The video is passed on exactly as the camera sends it (H.264 or H.265, no re-encoding, so it costs almost nothing), and a new viewer starts at once. Sound is shared when the camera sends AAC; G.711 sound is not (video only).
help.settings_share_turn_on_share: Turn on Share camera streams (off by default), choose the port (default 8554), then switch on each camera to share. Each shared camera shows its addresses with Copy buttons: rtsp://USER:PASSWORD@host:8554/camera_name is the main stream, adding /sub the sub stream (cameras that have one). Apps sign in with an AmberSight account (HTTP Basic, which is not encrypted: keep it on your own network or Tailscale); an account limited to some cameras only sees those, and anything not shared or not allowed looks like it does not exist. A password with special characters must be percent-encoded in the address (@ is %40).
help.settings_storage_segment_length_rec: Segment length: recordings are written in files of this many seconds. Retention: recordings older than this are deleted. Space for recordings: Automatic (the default) uses what the drive can spare and keeps 10% of it free (the percentage can be changed); Fixed size caps the data folder. Being full is normal: the oldest recordings make room. Folders, drives and the archive are set in Settings › Recording › Drives & folders.
help.settings_strangers_in_a_camera: In a camera's Alerts settings, Only alert for unknown people and vehicles keeps the camera quiet for people whose face you named (Settings › Smart features › Faces) and for vehicles whose plate you named (License plates). The events are still recorded and labeled; the AI review says why no alert was sent. An unknown face, an unknown plate, or someone whose face could not be identified (turned away, too far; or a car whose plate was not read) alerts, with a message such as "Unknown person at Front Door" or "Unknown car ABC123 in Driveway". Turn off Count people and vehicles that could not be identified as unknown to keep those quiet instead.
help.settings_strangers_with_only_during: With Only during hours (for example night) the filter applies inside them; outside, alerts are as usual, or none for people and vehicles. Alert only the first time stays quiet for an unknown person or plate that was already seen in the last days. For this the camera needs AI on, and faces and/or plates turned on; the alert waits a few seconds for the faces to be looked at (other cameras are not delayed).
help.settings_watchdog_it_never_acts: It never acts in the first 5 minutes after AmberSight starts, starts a new round at most once an hour per camera, and does nothing while most cameras are offline at once (that is the network or the power, not the cameras). While it works on a camera, the usual offline alert waits; if it cannot fix it, the alert says so.
help.settings_watchdog_turns_the_camera: Turns the camera watchdog on for every camera (each camera can be turned on or off on its own, Watchdog tab). Act after: minutes without video before it does anything. At most per day: restarts and power cycles per camera in 24 hours. Quiet hours: no restarts then (the offline alert still goes out).
help.share_clip_open_an_event: Open an event in Events: its clip plays, and the buttons under it download it. Tick several events (the box on each row) to download them together as a ZIP. On Live, the camera buttons save a snapshot and record a clip now (20 seconds); in playback, mark an in and out point and press E to export exactly that stretch. Protected events are never deleted automatically.
help.shortcuts_press_for_the: Press <kbd>?</kbd> for the full list. The most used: <kbd>1</kbd>-<kbd>9</kbd> open a camera full size, <kbd>F</kbd> full screen, <kbd>M</kbd> mute, <kbd>P</kbd> snapshot, <kbd>C</kbd> record a clip now, <kbd>S</kbd> arm / disarm, <kbd>T</kbd> timeline mode, <kbd>V</kbd> change the layout, <kbd>/</kbd> search events, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd><kbd>K</kbd> search everything, <kbd>G</kbd> then <kbd>E</kbd> (or <kbd>L</kbd><kbd>S</kbd><kbd>H</kbd>) go to a page, <kbd>Esc</kbd> close. In the timeline: <kbd>Space</kbd>/<kbd>K</kbd> play, <kbd>J</kbd><kbd>L</kbd> reverse/faster, <kbd>I</kbd><kbd>O</kbd> mark, <kbd>E</kbd> export, <kbd>End</kbd> live.
help.side_panel_the_panel_at: The panel at the side (open it with the button at the left of the Live toolbar) follows the selected camera. For a PTZ camera: hold the arrows (or the arrow keys) to move it, zoom, go to presets, or click a spot to center it / drag a box to zoom there. For a camera with a speaker: hold to talk. It also shows the active profile and the server's status.
help.start_in_the_header: In the header: the Armed / Disarmed button turns motion detection on or off for every camera at once; a colored dot shows the state of the server, and a chip appears when something needs attention (click it to see what). The sun/moon button picks the theme; the keyboard button lists keyboard shortcuts. The account button (the ... menu on a phone) holds theme (Auto follows your device, or Light, Dark), alert pop-ups, text size, start page, change password and sign out.
help.start_on_a_computer: On a computer the tabs across the top are Live (all cameras now, and playback), Events (what happened, as a list or a grid of clips), Time-lapse, Settings (administrators) and Help (this page). On a phone they are in a bar at the bottom: Live, Events, Settings and More (Time-lapse, Help, Keyboard shortcuts). A number on Events counts the events since you last opened it.
help.start_press_ctrl_k: Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> to search for a page, a setting, a camera or an action by name.
help.timelapse_a_whole_day: A whole day of one camera in a minute or so: one picture every so many seconds, played at 30 per second. Pick the camera and the day. When turned on (admins: the settings at the bottom of the tab), yesterday's is made each night for every recording camera or the ones chosen; Make now makes any day's, today's covering the day so far. They are kept for the days set (30 by default).
